Title: June 4, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Joint Public Hearing with Planning Board)

Topic1.Title: Call to Order and Roll Call
Topic1.Summary: Mayor Brockett called the special meeting of the Boulder City Council to order and staff conducted the roll call. All council members were present, and the mayor confirmed a quorum. The meeting was described as a joint session with the Planning Board, beginning with a council-only section.

Topic2.Title: Pride Month Declaration
Topic2.Summary: Council presented a proclamation declaring June 2026 as Pride Month and recognizing LGBTQ+ history, including the Stonewall uprising and local advocacy. Representatives from Rocky Mountain Equality accepted the declaration and spoke about Boulder's history of LGBTQ+ rights efforts. Council members thanked them and noted upcoming Boulder Pride events.

Topic3.Title: Points of Personal Privilege on a Student Group Letter
Topic3.Summary: Councilmember Lester read a statement condemning a letter from Boulder Students for Justice in Palestine that appeared to justify a 2025 terror attack that killed Karen Diamond and injured others. Mayor Pro Tem Winer read a statement from the District Attorney condemning the letter and affirming the sentence imposed on the attacker. Council members expressed support for condemning hate and antisemitism.

Topic4.Title: Consent Agenda Approval
Topic4.Summary: Council considered consent agenda items 2A through 2F with no discussion. A motion to approve was made and seconded, and a roll call vote was taken. The consent agenda was approved unanimously.

Topic5.Title: Opening of Joint Public Hearing on the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan
Topic5.Summary: Council opened the public hearing on the recommended major update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan, which is a joint hearing with the Planning Board. Planning Board Chair Laura Kaplan called the Planning Board meeting to order, confirmed a quorum with six of seven members present, and stated the purpose of the joint hearing. Mayor Brockett then resumed chairing the joint hearing and turned to staff for the presentation.

Topic6.Title: Staff Presentation on the Comprehensive Plan Update
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented the recommended major update to the comprehensive plan, the first of two approval sessions. Staff described the process, which included over 70 engagement opportunities, more than 1,000 public comments, and revisions to policies and the future land use map. Key changes included 104 plain-language policies, a simplified future land use strategy with 12 designations, and expanded focus on equity, housing, resilience, and open space. Staff also explained the approval sequence, noting that all four bodies must approve the same plan language and that substantive amendments would require reconciliation and possibly additional hearings.

Topic7.Title: Council and Planning Board Questions to Staff
Topic7.Summary: Council and Planning Board members asked staff about changes to the land use map, requesting a delta map before the next meeting. Questions addressed maintenance costs and funding, wildfire and evacuation risks in areas near the WUI, and how public amendments would be proposed and reconciled. Members also asked about residential uses in industrial designations, protections for existing industrial businesses, affordable housing targets, implementation and strategic planning, subcommunity and area planning, and groundwater protection. Staff clarified that the comprehensive plan sets high-level direction while zoning and future implementation determine specifics.

Topic8.Title: Public Hearing Testimony
Topic8.Summary: Seventeen speakers provided testimony, each limited to two or three minutes. Speakers raised concerns about public notification of land use changes, the survey methodology, and the removal of residential as a potential use in industrial designations. Others supported the plan's innovation economy focus, expressed concern about middle-income housing, wildfire and water risks, and the impacts of density, and urged more specificity in policies. Several speakers also requested restoration of earlier neighborhood category distinctions and stronger commitments to affordable housing.

Topic9.Title: Post-Testimony Clarifications and Continuance Motions
Topic9.Summary: Staff confirmed that the notification process through utility billing met legal requirements and clarified the origins and vetting of the survey questions. Planning Board voted 7-0 to continue its deliberation and action on the plan to June 16, 2026. Council voted unanimously to continue its deliberation and action to June 25, 2026, and the meeting was adjourned.
